draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Chettinad, the land of the Chettiars! This cluster of villages grew rich on trade as far away as Burma, Ceylon, Vietnam and Malaysia. Here in Kanadukathan, look at the house entrances, they're shaped to resemble temple gateways.
draft.hungryLine: Kanadukathan is famous for Chettinad cuisine, so you're in exactly the right place to eat it at the source.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Wander the lanes of Kanadukathan to see its grand houses with temple-style entrances. Chettinad railway station is just a 2 min walk if you're heading on to Karaikudi.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take it slow and stroll Kanadukathan's quiet streets, picking out the doorways of the old mansions one by one.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Chettinad once had 96 villages, but by 2010 only 74 were left, spread over about 1,550 square kilometres.

legends.title: The Shivaratri kavadi walk
legends.body: During Shivaratri in March, people carry kavadi from Pazhaiyur, old Kanadukathan, to the Solai Andavar Temple. It's a walk of roughly 4 km.

legends.title: Festival of the Goddess of Beauty
legends.body: Every May the town celebrates Ponnazhagi Amman for 10 days. Hari Poojai is held in May too.

tips.title: Visit in April or May for festivals.
tips.body: The Ponnazhagi Amman festival and the Nagamuthu Mariamman temple's Chithirai full moon festival both run for 10 days around then.

tips.title: Use Karaikudi as your base.
tips.body: Karaikudi is the urban centre for the Chettinad villages, and Chettinad lies on National Highway 536 between Trichy and Karaikudi.

story.title: Part of Pandya Nadu
story.body: Chettinad was historically ruled by the Ramnad kingdom of Pandya Nadu. Its name joins Chettiar, a community of traders and landlords, with nadu, meaning land.

story.title: Traders overseas
story.body: In the 19th and early 20th centuries, many Chettinad residents traded across South and Southeast Asia, especially in Burma, Ceylon, Vietnam and Malaysia.

story.title: 74 of 96 villages
story.body: Only 74 of the original 96 villages remained by 2010, in clusters across Sivagangai and Pudukottai districts.

story.title: Palatial houses on the world stage
story.body: Chettinad is part of a UNESCO nomination for palatial house sites of historic and cultural value. Kanadukathan is still best known for its food and its temple-like doorways.
